FINDINGS:

Five branches cut from the same commit all add an entry to the same top section of `CHANGELOG.md`. Their edits overlap, so sequential merges can conflict on that shared insertion area. With five branches, up to 10 branch pairs overlap; when merging them one by one, four merges can conflict after the first branch lands.

The cheapest durable fix is to give each task a unique changelog fragment path, such as `changelog.d/<task-id>.md`, and assemble those fragments into `CHANGELOG.md` during release. Each worker can add its fragment as part of the task’s existing edit, without coordinating on a shared file. Distinct paths avoid changelog merge conflicts as parallel branches grow, while keeping the per-task tool-call count to one edit call. Avoid appending to the end of the same file: parallel appends can conflict too.

Evidence: `CHANGELOG.md` has version entries at the top, the shared insertion point. `app/merge_operations.py` runs the worker merge through `execute_merge_session`; I found no changelog-specific merge handling or entry-generation workflow in the inspected project files.

Independent check: Git’s merge machinery can be used to compare merges of shared-file insertions with merges of distinct fragment paths. I attempted a read-only `git merge-file` simulation using process substitution, but it produced no output, so that check was inconclusive. The proposed fragment workflow still needs a successful merge simulation or CI check before adoption.
